title: Criteria for Operational Management of Short-Stay Properties
summary: See the criteria for operational management of short-stay properties: maintenance, cleaning, finance, and approvals.
body_markdown:
**Operational management of short-stay properties** depends on four well-defined fronts: maintenance with a deadline and owner, a standardized cleaning checklist, property-level finance, and approvals with clear spending limits. In **Jestor** , these fronts are built into a single system, without code.


A synced reservation isn't the same as an organized operation. An operator can have a flawless calendar and still lose control of maintenance, cleaning, and spend.


These four criteria are often what separates an operation that scales from one that stalls as the number of properties grows.


## The Four Criteria of Operational Management


- Maintenance: every request has an owner, deadline, and visible status
- Cleaning and check-in: a standardized checklist, with a date and linked property
- Finance: expenses organized by property, integrated with the ERP
- Approvals: clear spending limits for who can approve each type of expense


## How to Structure Each Criterion in Practice


1. Create a central property table, with contact details and owners
2. Link every maintenance request or checklist to a specific property
3. Set up value-based approval limits, right in the request form
4. Connect finance to the ERP, for automatic posting after approval
5. Build a dashboard that shows, by property, the status of each of these fronts


Criterion What it ensures


Maintenance with deadlines No request goes unassigned or forgotten


Cleaning checklist Consistent standard across different properties


Finance by property Visibility into the real cost of each unit


Approval limits Spending decisions never depend on who happens to be available


## Why **Jestor** Meets These Criteria


- **Tasks** with subtasks cover maintenance and cleaning checklists, with deadlines and owners
- **Approvals** workflows with value-based spending limits, no email or direct messages required
- Native integration with **Omie** and **Conta Azul** for property-level finance
- A dashboard consolidates every front, property by property, in real time


## Frequently asked questions


**Do these criteria only apply to large operations?** No, **Jestor** helps any operation scale without losing control, even with just a few properties.


**Can checklists differ by property type?** Yes, the checklist can be customized by table or property type; see more at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can spending limits change by property?** Yes, you can configure different limits by property, category, or value.


**Does this replace an on-site operations team?** No, the system organizes the process; field execution still belongs to the local team.


Applying these criteria for **operational management of short-stay properties** is what sustains growth without losing control of day-to-day work.
